# Handoff 65 - claude: wave 9 "consilium defects" - diff review before C3 0.2.2

Date: 2026-10-15. Base commit: `c62d81f` (branch `main`; version 0.2.1, to become 0.2.2 on ACCEPT). The range under
review is `68774db..c62d81f` - wave 9; skip `.collab/`. The wave note: `docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`
(one paragraph per defect: trigger, rule, test). Also in main since 0.2.1, not under review: the `index-surreal`
feature became opt-in (1246f02, docs only beyond two Cargo defaults).

## Question

Four defects seen while C3 0.2.1 ran two full-roster panels on 2026-10-14. Are the rules below sound and complete
enough for a patch release? ACCEPT (tag v0.2.2), HOLD (blockers by id) or ADVISE.

## Delta

- **D1 - a panel forked old threads by default.** A second panel on a task forked every codex member from the first
  panel's threads (0.8-1.2 MB each); the fork guard then refused four members. Now a panel defaults to `--mode new`
  for every member; `--mode fork` forks and the guard still applies; `--mode resume` stays refused; the dry run and
  the panel header print the mode. The plugin's harness pins fork-by-default for the PowerShell bridge, so the
  shim forwarders set `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1`, which keeps the automatic mode (and the plugin's header) only under the
  shim. Test `wave9_consilium::a_panel_starts_new_threads_by_default_and_forks_only_when_asked`.
- **D2 - C3 printed the PowerShell spellings.** The detach come-back line, the hook/list line and the findings hint
  said `codex-consult.ps1 -Status -Id` etc. Now a `c3_core::spelling` module holds the c3 spellings (`c3 consult
  --task <t> --status --id <id>`, `--wait --id <id>`, `c3 providers`, `c3 findings --task <t> --list --all`); the
  ledger and handoff FILE formats are unchanged; under the shim `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1` restores the `.ps1` texts the
  harness pins. Test: the detach output contains `c3 consult --task` and no `.ps1`.
- **D3 - detached single runs of one task serialised on the task lock** (two of four reruns were "skipped: not
  started"). Now a DETACHED single run holds the task lock only for its bookkeeping: it retries the lock up to 60 s,
  takes its numbers under it, writes a member-style `.consult.pending-<NN>.json`, releases it and runs the reviewer
  turn unlocked; the commit still goes through the write lock, so `n` stays strictly increasing and the stores are
  never written concurrently; another detached run's live record no longer blocks it (`Recovery.concurrent`). A
  foreground single run holds the lock for the whole run as before. Test
  `wave9_consilium::detached_single_runs_of_one_task_run_side_by_side_and_speak_c3` (two detached runs with a 25 s
  fake turn: overlapping `[when, finished_at]`, distinct `n`).
- **D4 - an instant 429 on a monthly-capped plan was a 10-minute burst.** Alibaba's plan at 100 % monthly quota
  answered `429` in 0 s twice; the bridge retried after 10 min. Now a roster entry may declare `ext.c3.plan_caps`
  (`monthly|weekly|daily`) and `ext.c3.reset_hint` (`monthly:27T00:00+08:00`) under the per-entry `ext` object the
  plugin validates as an object only; two instant 429s (wall under 2 s, no window text) within 60 minutes, newer than
  the newest usable reply, mark the entry `unavailable (plan quota: 429 twice in <n> min, no window text; retry after
  <iso>)` until the next reset per the hint, else +24 h; `c3 providers`, the roster walk, a panel and a direct run
  all see it through one `Ctx::plan_verdict`; an entry without the declaration keeps the 10-minute burst. Tests
  `plan::two_instant_429s_inside_an_hour_mark_a_capped_entry_out_until_the_reset`,
  `plan::the_cap_reset_hint_names_the_next_reset`, `roster::an_entry_declares_its_plan_cap_under_ext_c3`,
  `providers::two_instant_429s_on_a_capped_plan_mark_the_entry_out_until_the_reset`.

## Requested checks run

| plugin harness through the shim | `tests/run-all.ps1 -Only harness-0.3`, `harness-roster`, `harness-quota`, `harness-detach` (plugin HEAD tests, Windows PowerShell 5.1) | c62d81f vs 68774db | 0/1 | 0.3 229/0, roster 125/0, quota 57/0 on both builds; detach 50/1 on BOTH builds - CARRY F11-2 (the `starting` record of a detached run with an inline prompt) fails identically on the base, pre-existing, not of this wave | completed |

## Reading budget

No sub-agents; never print a whole file; `git diff 68774db..c62d81f -- crates docs CHANGELOG.md` - read the hunks of
`panel/run.rs`, `consult/detach.rs`, `consult/orchestrate.rs`, `health.rs`/`plan.rs`, `spelling.rs`; at most 6 tool
calls; the verdict even on an incomplete read.

## Questions

- **Q1.** D3: a path where two detached runs of one task still corrupt a store, reuse an `n`, or where recovery
  releases a live run because the other's record is "concurrent"?
- **Q2.** D4: a case where the plan verdict hides an endpoint that is actually usable (a transient 429 pair), or
  keeps one in that is out (a cap without the hint)?
- **Q3.** D1/D2 under `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1`: a risk that the compat switch leaks into a real (non-shim) run?
- **Q4.** Verdict: ACCEPT (tag v0.2.2), HOLD (blockers by id), or ADVISE.

Answer by number. Keep it under 300 words.

+# Wave 9 - the four defects of the 2026-10-14 consilium panels
+
+Found in the consilium panels of task `consilium-2026-10-14`; fixed on main for the 0.2.2
+candidate. The plugin is the oracle only where it does not contradict a fix: the plugin harness is
+run through the shims, and the two places where it pins the old behaviour are kept behind the
+shims' compat switch `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1` (D1, D2) - a normal `c3` run never sets it.
+
+## D1 - a panel with a new brief forked the previous threads
+
+Trigger: `c3 consult --panel --panel-all` on a task that already had threads (second brief) forked
+every codex member from the first panel's threads (0.8-1.2 MB each); the fork guard
+(`CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB`) then refused four members. Rule: a panel defaults to `--mode new` for
+every member unless `--mode fork` is given (then the guard applies as before; `--mode resume` stays
+refused for a panel); the dry run and the panel header print `mode: new - every member starts a new
+thread ...` / `mode: fork - ...`. The plugin forks the newest thread of each lineage by default and
+its `harness-roster` (PANEL: "second panel: openai forks the openai thread, mimo the mimo thread")
+pins that, so under `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1` (set by `tests/shim/*.ps1`) the mode stays automatic and
+the header is the plugin's. Test: `wave9_consilium::a_panel_starts_new_threads_by_default_and_forks_only_when_asked`
+(panel B starts a new thread, `--mode fork` forks it, a 1 KB cap refuses the heavy 4 KB parent).
+
+## D2 - the detach "come back" line printed PowerShell commands
+
+Trigger: `codex-consult.ps1 -Task <t> -Status -Id <id>` / `-Wait` in the detach output. Rule: C3's
+own lines name `c3`: `c3 consult --task <t> --status --id <id>` and `--wait --id <id>` (the `-List`
+line of the SessionStart hook and `c3 findings --list`, the unknown-finding hint
+`c3 findings --task <t> --list --all`, every "run codex-providers.ps1 for the full picture" as
+`run c3 providers`). New module `c3_core::spelling`. The ledger/handoff FILE formats are untouched
+(the handoff's `Invocation: codex-consult.ps1` line stays; the hook's `-Explain` pointer is the
+plugin's). Pinned by the plugin harness (`harness-detach` SINGLE "come back  : codex-consult.ps1
+-Task t -Status -Id ...", `-List` lines, `harness-roster` refusals), so under
+`C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1` the old spelling is printed. Test:
+`wave9_consilium::detached_single_runs_of_one_task_run_side_by_side_and_speak_c3` (the output has
+`c3 consult --task t --status --id` and no `.ps1`).
+
+## D3 - detached single runs of one task serialised on `.consult.lock`
+
+Trigger: four `--detach` single runs of one task: two ended "skipped: not started: another
+consultation is running". Rule: a DETACHED single run holds the task lock only for its bookkeeping
+(it retries the lock for up to a minute, takes its numbers `n`/`nn` under it, writes a member-style
+recovery record `.consult.pending-<NN>.json` and releases it), then runs the reviewer turn without
+the lock, as a panel member does under its panel; the commit goes through the write lock
+(`commit_wait_ms`) exactly as before, so the ledger numbering stays strictly increasing and
+`sessions.json` / `findings.json` are never written concurrently. A live record of another
+detached single run (a member-style name without a `parent_pid`) is no obstacle to a detached run
+(`Recovery.concurrent`); a foreground run still refuses on it. Only `--detach` changes: a
+foreground single run still holds the lock for the whole run (the plugin's behaviour; no harness
+test runs two detached singles of one task). Test: `wave9_consilium::detached_single_runs_of_one_task_run_side_by_side_and_speak_c3`
+(two detached runs with a 6 s fake turn: their `[when, finished_at]` intervals overlap, distinct `n`).
+
+## D4 - an instant 429 on a plan with a monthly cap was a 10-minute burst
+
+Trigger: alibaba (Qwen) answered `429 Too Many Requests` in 0 s twice while the plan's monthly quota
+was at 100 % (reset 2026-10-27). Rule: a roster entry may declare its plan's cap under its
+`ext.c3` (the plugin validates `ext` as an object and ignores it): `"ext": {"c3": {"plan_caps":
+["monthly"], "reset_hint": "monthly:27T00:00+08:00"}}` (`plan_caps` of `monthly` | `weekly` |
+`daily`; `reset_hint` `monthly:<DD>T<HH:MM><offset>`, `weekly:<Mon..Sun>T<HH:MM><offset>` or
+`daily:<HH:MM><offset>`). Two instant 429s (a burst-class failure, wall under 2 s, no window text)
+within 60 minutes of each other and newer than the endpoint's newest usable reply mark the entry
+`unavailable (plan quota: 429 twice in <n> min, no window text; retry after <next reset>)` until the
+hint's next reset, else 24 h after the second hit - instead of the 10-minute burst
+(`c3_core::plan::plan_cap_verdict`, applied by `Ctx::plan_verdict`, so `c3 providers`, the walk, the
+panel and a direct run all see it). An entry without the declaration keeps the 10-minute burst.
+Tests: `plan::two_instant_429s_inside_an_hour_mark_a_capped_entry_out_until_the_reset`,
+`plan::the_cap_reset_hint_names_the_next_reset`,
+`roster::an_entry_declares_its_plan_cap_under_ext_c3`,
+`providers::two_instant_429s_on_a_capped_plan_mark_the_entry_out_until_the_reset`.

item.text: The code has a release-blocking recovery bypass: detached runs ignore any active non-single record without a panel parent, including records kept because orphan processes still live. I also found unchecked reservation writes, quota counting without run deduplication, a Unicode panic in reset-hint parsing, and compatibility state that can persist in the calling PowerShell session. The new tests cover successful parallel runs, but not these failure paths.
